name: m4-chunked-uniques

variantDescriptions.weak: [retronym/scala#239](https://github.com/retronym/scala/pull/239) at `4192d5b9ca` with today's layout: `Types.uniques` in a `WeakHashSet`
variantDescriptions.chunked-weak: the same build with `ChunkedInterner(weak = true)`: open addressing over 64K-slot chunks, a slim `WeakReference` per type, tombstones; free-slot reuse and used-slot accounting fixes; growth at 1/4
variantDescriptions.chunked: the same build with `ChunkedInterner(weak = false)`: chunked table holding types strongly until the run discards it, no object per element

description: Scala 2 port of the chunked type interner ([retronym/scala#239](https://github.com/retronym/scala/pull/239), from retronym/scala3#117). Does keeping the `uniques` table out of G1's humongous regions cut young-GC card scanning for scalac as it did for dotc? Read `cyc%:gc` and time; instructions/op should be near flat. Layout chosen per variant with `-Dscala.uniques.layout` (what `-Yuniques-layout:default` reads), one build. Same setup as `m4-forkvar-uniques`: scala corpus, 8 GB heap, separate forks, no forced GC, patched JDK 26, M4.

Scala 3 reference on the M4: [hashcons-scalaz-sized](../../scala3-2d50b0/ab/index.html#c-hashcons-scalaz-sized) (scalaz, chunked-weak −2.9% time, GC 29.1% → 9.3% of cycles) and `hashcons-scalaz-fixes` (job 538, the same fixes as this build). Explainer: https://claude.ai/artifact/NWGiMojrz2W4VDLqAKbq6B
